about: REQ-356 — what every new site plan starts with.
DATA AND NOT CODE, so the list can change without a code change. The decisions
are [[DOC-64]] §6 and the standing checks are §7; this file is that document's
two tables, in the shape the plan stores them. A plan is seeded once, when it is
first written, so editing this file changes plans created afterwards and leaves
existing ones as they are.
`settle` is how the decision is expected to be settled — asked, talked through,
shown, or offered ([[DOC-64]] §3.1). It tells the coordinator how to raise it.
`triggers` name the moments a check fires ([[DOC-64]] §7). Firing them is the
coordinator's runtime and out of scope here; the names are recorded so that
runtime has something to match on.
[[REQ-379]], [[REQ-399]] — `feature_catalogue` is the fixed list of what a
site can DO, one functional capability per entry: content sections (reviews,
hours, prices) are page structure and the consultant's to settle, and are not
here. `available` says whether the framework builds it yet, and is said in this
one place, so shipping a module is a one-line flip. An unavailable capability is
still offered, marked, because wanting it is the signal for what to build next.
`features_ask` is the wording of the features question. It is NOT SEEDED: the
consultant raises it with `ask_features` once she has some context, choosing
which capabilities to offer, which to tick in advance, and how to word each for
the business. Answering it fills the plan's `functionality`, by capability id.
`asks` are the panel questions a new plan starts with, and there are none.
[[REQ-390]] — `stages` are the build's stages as the client's tracker shows
them, in the order it shows them (operator-approved wording). The consultant
marks each not started, in progress or done, in any order. A new plan starts
with the first in progress.
[[REQ-398]] — `about` is each stage's one-sentence explanation, in the
client's words; the progress banner shows it on hover and writes none itself.
[[REQ-405]] — each stage's finish line, what the consultant steers the client
to before ticking it done, is in `priming.json`'s plan-panel paragraph (both
variants). It is consultant guidance, not client wording, so it lives there; a
stage added, renamed or dropped here changes there too.
[[REQ-403]] — `opening` is the consultant's first message in every new
conversation, one markdown line per entry. It is stock text, not a model turn:
the client releases it with Click here to start, and it walks through the
stages above, so the two are kept side by side and change together.
[[REQ-408]] — the `weakest_point` check falls due after the first draft and when
Publish opens. Asking it needs a judgement of the draft against the
distinctiveness rubric in `priming.json`'s conduct paragraph, so the rubric is
applied when it is due rather than whenever the prompt is remembered. A check
added here reaches existing plans on their next read (`plan.ts`).
[[REQ-416]] — `story_areas` are the parts a small business's story usually
has, as the consultant's priming lists them. Each pinned note may name the area
it belongs to; an area with no note on the board is one the consultant has not
asked about yet, and the talker's reminder lists those while a build runs.

focus.about: REQ-424 — guided focus tasks. A story-board reaction task covers at most this many notes, so the client is never handed the whole board at once; the rest wait, marked new, for the next task.
focus.about_unreacted: REQ-428 — with more than this many new notes (pinned, no reaction, covered by no story task) pin_notes is refused until a reaction task has run over them.

stages.label: Getting to know you
stages.about: We learn about your business, your customers and what you want the site to do.

stages.label: Looking at other sites
stages.about: We look at sites you like, and some you don't, to find the style that suits you.

stages.label: First draft
stages.about: We build a first version of your site so you have something real to react to.

stages.label: Refining
stages.about: We work through your feedback on the pages, the words and the pictures until they feel right.

stages.label: Colours & fonts
stages.about: We settle the colours and the lettering so the site looks like your business.

stages.label: Finishing touches
stages.about: We check every page, link and form and tidy up the last details.

stages.label: Ready to publish
stages.about: Your site is finished and ready to go live whenever you say.

opening: Hello — I'm here to design and build your website with you. I'll give you my honest opinion as we go, but it's your site, so you always have the final say.

**How we'll get there.** The progress bar at the top of the panel shows the steps: getting to know your business, looking at other sites, a first draft, refining, colours and fonts, finishing touches, and then ready to publish. I'll build a first draft early, so you have something real to react to, and we'll carry on getting to know your business while it's built. We can move around freely — just tell me what you'd like to look at.
- **The questions panel** above this chat collects simple facts, like your phone number and opening hours. Fill them in whenever suits you.
- **The story board** (Story, beside the preview) is where I pin the things you tell me about your business, in your own words. Heart the ones that are most you.
- **The preview** shows your site as it's built. **View on your phone** shows it the way most of your customers will see it.

- **Before a long piece of work,** I'll tell you, and roughly how long it will take. **While I build, keep talking to me** — that's when I'll hear your story, and what you tell me goes into the next pass.
- **When I show you several looks,** tell me which you prefer.
- **Photos, your logo, flyers** — upload anything you have. It all helps.
So, to start: tell me about your business. What do you do, and who are your customers?
